tb21_profile.skill: Make a numerical simulation run at least 40% faster by changing only its configuration (solver, integrator, iteration/tolerance settings, disabled features, collision pruning) while the full physics state stays within atol=1e-5 of the reference and never goes NaN/Inf - i.e. measure, hypothesise, change one knob, re-measure against a supplied eval script
tb21_profile.domain: MuJoCo / MJCF XML, rigid-body physics simulation, numerical integrators and constraint solvers, wall-clock profiling
tb21_profile.task_form: optimise-for-a-budget with a hard numerical-equivalence constraint; edit a declarative config rather than write code, and iterate against a provided eval harness

notes: The new corpora beat the old ones here, but less overwhelmingly than on the fastText and distributed-PyTorch tasks, and TMax is a genuine second. MuJoCo itself is essentially absent from the pool: a regex for mujoco|mjcf|physics engine|rigid body over all 56,307 v1 instructions returns 5 hits (4 generic TMax 'physics engine' fictions plus tw_471679, which only installs MuJoCo 2.1.0), and over the 20,479 new-corpus instructions it returns zero. So nobody can supply the domain. What CalibForge supplies instead, and supplies far better than anything in v1, is the task_form: a large, strongly-verified 'optimization' and 'scientific-computing' family whose tasks are literally 'this simulation is too slow, make it hit a time target while its numbers still match a reference to a stated tolerance', several of which even ship an /app/eval.py to iterate against. scientific-computing_20260604_003814_008 is the standout - under 2 seconds, error below 1e-8, iterate with eval.py - and CalibForge additionally has three integrator/energy-drift tasks (DOPRI5 error control, velocity-Verlet+SHAKE, N-body drift) that are the nearest thing to reasoning about a physics solver's accuracy-versus-cost knobs. Eight of my final ten are CalibForge and two are TMax; TMax's speedup-with-identical-output cluster (10x, 3x, burst-of-100) is real and I would not drop it. Corpora where I could not find ten defensible candidates: TerminalWorld (its two on-domain tasks are an MBDyn build graded FREE by the packet and a MuJoCo pip install; ranks 6-10 are benchmark-adjacent filler) and Recursive-Task-Synthesis (nothing above overall 2 - its best is 'check measured runtimes against thresholds in a conf file', and everything is `absent`). SWE-Rebench is also weak; I picked the physical-simulation frameworks (PyBaMM, OpenMDAO, arch) and benchmarking-methodology issues (benchopt warm_up, smac3) over the lexically-retrieved noise, but nothing there exceeds overall 2. One deliberate non-obvious call: I ranked the SWE-Smith cantools/ARXML cluster first in that corpus because MJCF is a declarative XML description of a physical system, and those tasks are the only place in the pool where someone must reason about the semantics of such a file rather than about code.
